issues.description: Check class name and file path disagree with the metadata's stated intent (single vs multiple)
issues.detail: The PR title and description say this check detects VMs with multiple network interfaces, but the CheckID, file/directory name, and class are all `compute_instance_single_network_interface`. That inverts the natural reading: a check named 'single_network_interface' that FAILs when the property holds is asymmetrically wrong. Either rename to `compute_instance_multiple_network_interfaces` (matching the PR title and the changelog entry shown in the description) or change the semantics so PASS means 'single' and the name reads as a positive assertion. Pick one; do not ship both spellings.

issues.description: GKE classification by `name.startswith("gke-")` is a fragile heuristic, not an invariant
issues.detail: The check decides MANUAL vs FAIL based on whether the instance name begins with the literal string `gke-`. That is a naming convention, not a guarantee: users can name any VM `gke-foo`, and conversely GKE node names can be customized in some configurations. A correct audit would inspect labels (e.g. `goog-gke-node`), metadata, or the managed instance group, not the display name. As written, this is an attacker-controllable evasion: name your bridging VM `gke-anything` and the check downgrades FAIL to MANUAL. Document the limitation in metadata.Notes at minimum, and prefer a label-based check.

issues.description: Dead-branch path: `interface_count == 0` cannot occur for a valid GCE Instance, yet the code handles it silently as PASS
issues.detail: GCE instances must have at least one network interface; `networkInterfaces` is never empty in practice. The else-branch sets a status_extended saying 'no network interfaces' but leaves `report.status = "PASS"` from the top of the loop. That is misleading: if the invariant were ever violated, a zero-NIC instance would silently pass a check whose purpose is to count NICs. Either drop the branch (and assert the invariant in `_get_instances`), or set status to `MANUAL`/`FAIL` with a clear message. State the invariant in a comment so the next reader understands why the branch is or isn't there.

issues.description: `interface_names` is computed unconditionally but only used on two of three branches
issues.detail: `interface_names = [nic.name for nic in instance.network_interfaces]` is built before the branching, which is fine and O(k) where k is small, so the cost is negligible. Not a performance issue (premature optimization to fix), but worth one line of literate comment stating the loop invariant: `report.status` starts at PASS and is downgraded to FAIL or MANUAL based on `interface_count`; `interface_names` is purely for the human-readable message. A reader should not have to reconstruct that.

issues.description: Tests do not cover the documented `interface_count == 0` branch
issues.detail: The check has three branches (==1, >1, else). The test file covers single, two, three, four, and GKE-multi, but never the zero-NIC case. If the empty branch is intentional defensive code, a test should pin its behavior; if it is dead code, it should be removed. Either way, the test suite should match the branch structure of the code under audit.

issues.description: Service-layer parsing silently drops the network/subnetwork path information
issues.detail: In `_get_instances`, `interface.get("network", "").split("/")[-1]` keeps only the final path component of the resource URL. For a check that exists to reason about cross-network bridging, the fully-qualified network URL (which encodes the project) is the load-bearing identifier; two different projects can have networks named `default`. The current check only counts NICs so it doesn't bite today, but a follow-up check that wants to detect 'NICs spanning different VPC projects' would be misled by this lossy truncation. Consider storing both the short name and the full self-link, or document the choice in a comment.

review.summary: UNDER-AUDITED with a NEEDS-LITERATE-COMMENT smell. The algorithm is trivial — count `instance.network_interfaces`, branch on the count — and its complexity is plainly O(N*k) where N is instances and k is the (tiny) NIC count, so there is nothing to optimize. The real defects are not performance but rigor: (1) the check is named and filed as `single_network_interface` while the PR, changelog phrasing, and FAIL semantics describe a 'multiple_network_interfaces' check; pick one spelling. (2) The GKE exemption is implemented by string-prefix match on the display name, which is an attacker-controllable heuristic, not an invariant — labels would be the correct signal. (3) The zero-NIC branch is unreachable for valid GCE instances yet silently returns PASS, and no test pins its behavior; state the invariant or delete the branch. The service-layer change is fine, modulo a minor concern that truncating network/subnetwork URLs to the last path component throws away project context that a future cross-project bridging check will want. Nothing here blocks merge on correctness of the single check, but the naming inversion and the GKE heuristic deserve fixes before this becomes a precedent other GCP checks copy.
